data.title: Digisible number
data.statement:
A positive integer is called <<digisible>> if it meets all three of the following conditions:

1. No zero digits — None of its digits is 0.

2. All digits are unique — No digit appears more than once.

3. Divisible by each digit — The number is evenly divisible by every one of its digits.

Example: 124 is digisible because:

Digits: 1, 2, 4 (no zeros)

All digits are unique

124 ÷ 1 = 124, 124 ÷ 2 = 62, 124 ÷ 4 = 31 (all integers)

Example: 123 is not digisible because:

123 ÷ 2 = 61.5 (not divisible by digit 2)

Given an integer [[N]], output the failed condition and the next digisible number <<greater or equal to>> [[N]]
data.outputDescription:
Failure reasons (combine as needed):
ZERO — contains digit 0

DUPLICATE — contains duplicate digits

DIVISIBLE — not divisible by at least one digit

Combine with + if multiple conditions fail.
And the next digisible number <<greater than or equal to>> [[N]]

Goal

A positive integer is called digisible if it meets all three of the following conditions:

1. No zero digits — None of its digits is 0.

2. All digits are unique — No digit appears more than once.

3. Divisible by each digit — The number is evenly divisible by every one of its digits.

Example: 124 is digisible because:

Digits: 1, 2, 4 (no zeros)

All digits are unique

124 ÷ 1 = 124, 124 ÷ 2 = 62, 124 ÷ 4 = 31 (all integers)

Example: 123 is not digisible because:

123 ÷ 2 = 61.5 (not divisible by digit 2)

Given an integer N, output the failed condition and the next digisible number greater or equal to N
Input
A single integer N.
Output
Failure reasons (combine as needed):
ZERO — contains digit 0

DUPLICATE — contains duplicate digits

DIVISIBLE — not divisible by at least one digit

Combine with + if multiple conditions fail.
And the next digisible number greater than or equal to N
Constraints
num <= 999999
Example
Input
29354
Output
DIVISIBLE
29736
